title: Carbon monoxide and particulates from incomplete combustion
key_idea: When a fuel burns without enough oxygen, **incomplete combustion** produces toxic carbon monoxide and solid carbon particles called soot. Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless, so it is hard to detect, and it stops the blood carrying oxygen.

blocks.text: Burning a fuel is a reaction with oxygen. What forms depends on how much oxygen is available.

items.meaning: Burning with plenty of oxygen. A hydrocarbon forms carbon dioxide and water.
Burning with not enough oxygen. A hydrocarbon forms carbon monoxide and/or carbon, plus water.
Solid particles of carbon released when a fuel burns incompletely.
Tiny solid particles in the air, such as soot and unburned hydrocarbons.

items: Most fuels, including coal, contain carbon and/or hydrogen.
With limited oxygen, some of the carbon forms carbon monoxide instead of carbon dioxide.
Some carbon may not react at all. It is released as soot.

where: C is carbon, which is released as soot.

items: Complete combustion needs plenty of oxygen and makes carbon dioxide and water.
Incomplete combustion needs limited oxygen and makes carbon monoxide and/or soot, plus water.
Say not enough oxygen, never no oxygen.

blocks.text: Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas. This section covers why it is dangerous and how people are protected.

items: It is colourless and odourless, so people cannot see or smell it.
This means it is not easily detected before it does harm.
It is toxic.
Carbon monoxide detectors are placed near boilers and other appliances that burn fuel.

blocks.text: How it behaves as a poison

items: Carbon monoxide attaches to haemoglobin in red blood cells.
This reduces the amount of oxygen the blood can carry.
So less oxygen reaches the brain and other organs.
Effects include difficulty breathing, drowsiness and death.
Carbon monoxide is colourless, odourless and toxic.
It attaches to haemoglobin, so the blood carries less oxygen.
Detectors are needed because people cannot sense it.

blocks.text: Soot is the solid pollutant from incomplete combustion. Other solid particles and unburned hydrocarbons also form particulates.

items: Particulates cause global dimming, which means less sunlight reaches the Earth's surface.
Particulates cause health problems for humans.
In appliances such as boilers, incomplete combustion releases both soot and carbon monoxide.
Soot is solid carbon from incomplete combustion.
Particulates cause global dimming and health problems.

checks.q: Explain how carbon monoxide is produced when methane is burned.
checks.a: There is not enough oxygen, so the methane undergoes incomplete combustion.

checks.q: Name the solid pollutant and the gaseous pollutant formed when a hydrocarbon burns incompletely.
checks.a: The solid is soot (carbon) and the gas is carbon monoxide.

checks.q: Explain how carbon monoxide behaves as a toxic gas.
checks.a: It reacts with haemoglobin in red blood cells. This stops oxygen being carried by the blood, so less oxygen reaches the brain.

checks.q: Why are carbon monoxide detectors needed?
checks.a: Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless, so it cannot be detected by sight or smell, and it is toxic.

worked_example.question:
Some central heating boilers use methane as a fuel. Carbon monoxide detectors are placed near central heating boilers.

Which three properties of carbon monoxide make it necessary to use carbon monoxide detectors?

Choose answers from the box: acidic, alkaline, colourless, corrosive, insoluble, odourless, toxic
worked_example.tip: One mark for each correct property, in any order.

worked_example.question:
Pentadecane, C₁₅H₃₂, is a hydrocarbon and is used as a fuel.
The incomplete combustion of pentadecane produces carbon monoxide.
Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas.

Explain how carbon monoxide behaves as a toxic gas.
answer_points: Carbon monoxide reacts with haemoglobin in the blood, or with red blood cells.
This stops oxygen being carried by the haemoglobin or blood, so less oxygen reaches the brain.
worked_example.tip: The two marks need an explanation linking both points.

worked_example.question:
Atmospheric pollution can be caused by
• carbon monoxide
• oxides of nitrogen
• sulfur dioxide.

Explain why carbon monoxide in the atmosphere is a problem.
answer_points: Carbon monoxide is poisonous or toxic.
And one from: it can cause difficulty breathing or suffocation; it attaches to the haemoglobin in red blood cells; it reduces the amount of oxygen the blood can carry; it can cause drowsiness.
worked_example.tip: One mark for toxic and one mark for a specific effect.

worked_example.question: Give the name of the substance that is a product of incomplete combustion of fossil fuels.
worked_example.tip: Soot (carbon particulates) is also a product, but carbon monoxide is the substance this question wants.

items: Particulates from incomplete combustion increase the risk of **respiratory problems** and **cancer**.
Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas.

Other pollutants have other sources: methane comes from decomposing vegetation and waste gases from animal digestion, oxides of nitrogen from car engines, and sulfur dioxide from burning fossil fuels that contain sulfur compounds.

worked_example.question:
This question is about alkanes.

When an alkane burns in a limited supply of air, incomplete combustion occurs.

Explain why incomplete combustion of an alkane could be harmful to humans.
answer_points: Carbon monoxide is produced, and it is toxic (it reduces the capacity of the blood to carry oxygen).
Or: carbon (soot) is produced, and it causes asthma, bronchitis or respiratory problems.
One pair of linked points scores the two marks.
worked_example.tip: Name the product first, then say what it does. The second mark depends on the first.
